Threads

Source: R/threads.R
zl_threads.Rd

zl_threads() sets how many threads 'ggml' computes with, for every graph, trainer and gradient of the session, and returns the previous number; with no argument it returns the current one. It starts at 1. A request is capped at the number of available cores and, while R CMD check limits cores (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_), at 2: too many threads on too few cores make 'ggml' many times slower.

Usage

zl_threads(n = NULL)

Arguments

n

NULL, or the number of threads: a positive whole number.

Value

The number of threads; when setting, the previous number, invisibly.

Details

One pool of threads serves the session; it is recreated when the number changes, and in a process forked from this one. Results are identical at any number of threads (see the package documentation on determinism). A computation can be interrupted between two of its operations; it then signals a condition of class zulm_interrupt, which also inherits interrupt.

Examples

old <- zl_threads(2)
zl_threads()
#> [1] 2
zl_threads(old)
